transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I guess… I came in because I barely care about things anymore. Like, things that used to feel like me—dance class, hiking, trying new recipes. I used to make this lemon chicken thing all the time, my neighbor loved it, actually she’d ask for leftovers—but now even that feels like this big task.

And game night too. I’ll see the text and think, “Yeah, I should go,” but it just sits there like another chore I keep putting off. I don’t know, it’s like the interest is just… gone.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly, but most days there’s this… low feeling there. Like a sour feeling under everything. Fear, guilt, all mixed together, even when nothing is actually happening.

Like I’ll be washing a cup or trying to decide what to eat and it’s just there. I used to blame it on being tired, or the weather—my mom always says gray weather “gets in your bones,” which sounds dramatic but kind of true, I guess—but this feels like it’s there even on normal days. Just sitting underneath everything.
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or having low energy, even after resting or sleeping?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I get tired, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal, you know? Sometimes I sit down “for a minute” and then I’ve lost track of time, but then again I’ve always been kind of bad about that—my aunt used to say I could turn one cup of tea into a whole afternoon.

So… I haven’t really noticed a clear thing where sleep doesn’t help or anything. I guess I just haven’t been paying attention to it that way.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like dance class, hiking, or cooking?

Yeah… that’s kind of the main thing, I guess. I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Dance class, hiking, trying new recipes… even game night. They don’t feel fun anymore, they just sort of sit there like chores I keep putting off.

I’ll think, “I should go, I used to like this,” and then I just… don’t. Like my sneakers are still by the door from the last time I told myself I’d go on a hike, and I keep moving them when I vacuum instead of actually using them.
Have you been feeling guilty or felt like you’re not good enough for no clear reason lately?

Yeah… guilty, mostly. Not always about one specific thing, which is what makes it weird. It’s just kind of there most days, like this sour feeling under everything, fear and guilt mixed together.

Like I’ll be doing something normal—folding towels or standing in the cereal aisle way too long because there are too many kinds now, honestly—and suddenly I feel like I’ve done something wrong, or like I’m about to. But nothing is actually happening. It’s just… sitting there underneath everything.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately?

Um… appetite or weight? I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t really been tracking it. My scale is actually shoved under the bathroom cabinet behind this basket of hair stuff I never use, so it’s not like I check regularly.

Food-wise… I eat, I guess. Some days I forget until it’s late, but I’ve always been sort of weird with meals if I get distracted. Like I’ll start making toast and then notice the mail on the counter and suddenly I’m sorting coupons from three weeks ago. So… no big change that I’ve noticed, I don’t think.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slower than usual, or that you're moving more slowly, like everything is kind of in slow motion?

I don’t know… slower thoughts, like slow motion? I don’t think I’ve noticed that exactly.

Sometimes I’ll kind of stare at something longer than I mean to, but then I’m also the kind of person who loses ten minutes reading the back of a shampoo bottle in the shower, so I don’t know if that counts. Moving-wise, I don’t think anyone’s told me I’m slow or anything. I still get around okay, I guess.
Have you had trouble sleeping recently, like waking up in the middle of the night or not being able to fall asleep, or on the flip side, have you been sleeping much more than usual?

Sleep… I’m not sure. I mean, I sleep, but I haven’t really been paying attention to whether it’s more or less than usual.

I do remember last night I was trying to figure out if my sheets need replacing because one corner keeps popping off the mattress, and then I got annoyed thinking about fitted sheets in general—like who decided those elastic corners were enough? But I guess that’s not really what you asked.

I don’t know that it’s changed a lot. Some nights are better than others, but I couldn’t tell you if it’s a pattern.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough, or been overly hard on yourself lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if it’s “not good enough” exactly, but I keep going over it in my head.

Like, I keep telling myself I should’ve known better than to take that booking. And then I start thinking about all the little things I could’ve checked, or asked, or… I don’t know. It’s like when you buy something online and afterward all the bad reviews suddenly seem obvious, except this wasn’t a toaster or whatever.

I feel like I failed the people who were helping me. Like I should’ve kept them safe, and I didn’t. I know maybe that sounds dramatic, but that’s where my brain keeps going.
Have you noticed that you’re feeling more tired or that you’re lacking energy lately, even if you haven’t been doing much?

I’m not sure. I mean, I get tired sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal.

It’s hard to tell because some days I’ll sit down and suddenly realize I’ve been doing, like, nothing useful for an hour, but then I wonder if that’s tiredness or just… I don’t know, getting distracted. Like yesterday I meant to clean up the kitchen and somehow ended up sorting through a drawer full of old takeout menus, which I don’t even know why I still have because everything’s online now.

So… energy-wise, I guess I haven’t really noticed a big change. Nothing I can clearly point to.
Have you had experiences like this before, where you felt down or lost interest in things, or is this something that’s mostly new for you?

It’s mostly new, I think. I mean, I’ve had normal down patches before, everybody does, but this feels different.

That’s kind of why I came in… I barely care about the stuff that used to make me feel like me. Dance class, hiking, trying a new recipe, even game night with friends—it all just sits there now like some chore I keep putting off.

And it’s weird because I still have the hiking boots by the door, which is annoying because I keep tripping over them, and I keep thinking I should move them to the closet, but then that feels like admitting I’m not going. So they just stay there. But yeah… mostly new.
Can you think of a time recently when you noticed feeling more tired than usual, even if you weren’t doing much physically or mentally?

Um… I’m trying to think of a specific time, but nothing really stands out.

Like, I’ll have moments where I’m sitting there and I feel kind of drained, but then I can’t tell if that’s “tired” or if I just got stuck doing nothing. The other day I was on the couch with the TV on, but I wasn’t even watching it—there was some cooking show, I think, and they were making something with pears, which I don’t even like cooked, honestly.

But physically tired? More than usual? I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed a clear change like that.
Have you noticed a clear increase in fatigue or a loss of energy that stands out compared to how you usually feel, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally?

I don’t think so… not a clear increase, anyway.

I mean, I do have times where I feel kind of wiped out, but then I’ll think, well, maybe I just sat too long or didn’t eat a real lunch or got lost scrolling through stuff. Like my phone keeps showing me these little videos of people organizing their pantries, and somehow I’ll watch five of them even though my own pantry is a disaster.

But compared to my usual energy? I can’t really say there’s been some obvious drop. Nothing that stands out enough for me to point to and say, “yeah, that’s new.”
Has this low mood and loss of interest in things been happening nearly every day for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s been kind of most days, where I just don’t care about the things I used to actually look forward to.

Like dance class—I keep seeing the reminder on my calendar and then I just ignore it. And hiking, cooking, game night… it all feels like stuff I’m supposed to do, not stuff I want to do. Which is weird, because I used to be the one pushing people to try a new trail or some recipe I found online, even if it turned out terrible.

So… yes, it’s been going on for at least a couple weeks, I’d say. Mostly every day.
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately, even about small things?

Yeah… that one, yes. I notice it more when I’m trying to do paperwork.

Like I’ve been trying to work on these catering forms, and there’s this Chamber application too, and I’ll read the same line over and over and it just doesn’t… stick. Then I get hung up on tiny things, like what price I’m supposed to put down, or which email I should answer first.

And then somehow I’m looking at the paperclip on the desk or thinking I should reorganize the drawer, which is ridiculous because the forms are still sitting right there. So yeah, I guess concentrating and deciding has been harder lately.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight or a decrease in your appetite lately, even if you haven’t been tracking it closely?

I haven’t really noticed anything major like that. I mean, I don’t weigh myself much unless I’m at someone’s house that has a scale in the bathroom, and even then I usually forget why I went in there because they have fancy soaps or whatever.

My appetite’s kind of… normal, I think? Some days I snack instead of making an actual meal, but I’ve always done that when I don’t feel like cooking. Like I’ll eat crackers standing in the kitchen and call it dinner, which probably isn’t ideal, but it doesn’t feel like some big new change.

So no, I don’t think there’s been significant weight change or appetite loss that I’ve noticed.
Have you found yourself thinking a lot about death or dying, or wishing you could just not wake up?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly.

I mean, I don’t think I sit around planning anything, if that’s what you mean. But sometimes I do get kind of stuck on… like, the idea of being able to turn everything off for a while. Not in a dramatic way, just more like when your phone battery dies and you’re almost relieved because nobody can reach you—except then you remember you needed the directions or the grocery list or whatever.

Death as an actual thing… I don’t know. I try not to think about it too much. It makes me uncomfortable, and then my brain starts wandering to stuff like who would take care of my plants, which is stupid because half of them are already barely alive.

So… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’m thinking about it a lot, but I guess I have had those “I wish I could just not deal with anything” kind of thoughts sometimes.
Have you had any thoughts about ending your life or not wanting to be here anymore?

I don’t… I don’t think I can say it like that. Not “ending my life,” no, I don’t have some plan sitting there or anything.

Sometimes I get this feeling like I don’t want to be in my own day, if that makes sense? Like I want to step outside of it for a while, the way people take a sick day, except it’s not really a sick day because then you still have dishes and phone calls and those little appointment reminder cards that end up on the fridge forever.

But not wanting to be here anymore… I’m not sure. I don’t really think I mean it that way. It’s more like wanting everything to stop being so loud for a minute. So… no, not thoughts about actually ending my life.

I haven’t really noticed anything major like that. I mean, I don’t weigh myself much unless I’m at someone’s house that has a scale in the bathroom, and even then I usually forget why I went in there because they have fancy soaps or whatever.

My appetite’s kind of… normal, I think? Some days I snack instead of making an actual meal, but I’ve always done that when I don’t feel like cooking. Like I’ll eat crackers standing in the kitchen and call it dinner, which probably isn’t ideal, but it doesn’t feel like some big new change.

So no, I don’t think there’s been significant weight change or appetite loss that I’ve noticed.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has had recurrent thoughts of death or dying, which would help distinguish between the current candidate diagnoses.
doctor.question: Have you found yourself thinking a lot about death or dying, or wishing you could just not wake up?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thoughts of death, dying, or passive suicidal ideation, which is not covered by any item in the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly.

I mean, I don’t think I sit around planning anything, if that’s what you mean. But sometimes I do get kind of stuck on… like, the idea of being able to turn everything off for a while. Not in a dramatic way, just more like when your phone battery dies and you’re almost relieved because nobody can reach you—except then you remember you needed the directions or the grocery list or whatever.

Death as an actual thing… I don’t know. I try not to think about it too much. It makes me uncomfortable, and then my brain starts wandering to stuff like who would take care of my plants, which is stupid because half of them are already barely alive.

So… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’m thinking about it a lot, but I guess I have had those “I wish I could just not deal with anything” kind of thoughts sometimes.

doctor.intent: Assess the presence and frequency of suicidal ideation with a specific focus on whether the patient has had thoughts of ending their life, separate from general wishes to 'not deal' with things.
doctor.question: Have you had any thoughts about ending your life or not wanting to be here anymore?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is directly about suicidal ideation or not wanting to live, which is not covered by any item in the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I don’t… I don’t think I can say it like that. Not “ending my life,” no, I don’t have some plan sitting there or anything.

Sometimes I get this feeling like I don’t want to be in my own day, if that makes sense? Like I want to step outside of it for a while, the way people take a sick day, except it’s not really a sick day because then you still have dishes and phone calls and those little appointment reminder cards that end up on the fridge forever.

But not wanting to be here anymore… I’m not sure. I don’t really think I mean it that way. It’s more like wanting everything to stop being so loud for a minute. So… no, not thoughts about actually ending my life.
